newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Subic says Hutchison wins port deal.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Subic says Hutchison wins port deal.

text.p: The Philippines' Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) said on Tuesday its board of directors had again selected Hutchison Ports Philippines Ltd as the winning bidder to develop a container port terminal.
"The decision is subject to review by President Fidel Ramos, to whom it has been submitted," an SBMA statement said.
Hutchison is a unit of Hutchison Whampoa Ltd.
SBMA initially awarded the contract to Hutchison but the decision was challenged by one of the losing bidders, Philippine port operator International Container Terminal Services Inc.
President Fidel Ramos then ordered SBMA to re-evaluate the bidding and today's announcement was the result of that review.

ICTSI's oridinal bid was rejected on the grounds that it would violate a law forbidding monopolies in the port industry. ICTSI operates the Manila International Container Terminal which handles 70 percent of container traffic in the country.
The SBMA board said that in the review it based its decision purely on the financial returns each of the competing bidders had offered.
"This greatest financial return is not an arbitrary figure quoted by the bidder but should be supported by a valid or realistic business plan," SBMA said in a statement.

It said it rejected ICTSI's contention that the only financial factor that should be looked into was royalty per twenty-foot-equivalent unit (TEU). In the original bidding in August, ICTSI gave the highest royalty of $58 per TEU, followed by Hutchison with $20.50 and Germany's Royal Port Services with $15.00.
In its bid, Hutchison said it planned to build new wharfs at Subic in the fourth year which would effectively increase the number of ship calls at a faster pace.

ICTSI had set the construction of new wharfs only in the ninth year. ICTSI had offered a higher royalty because it would raise its rates and charges by 10 percent yearly for the first two years and 5.0 percent thereafter, the SBMA had said.
SBMA said it hired three independent port experts to evaluate the bids. Representatives of the government's Commission on Audit were also present to review the bids.
SBMA Chairman Richard Gordon voluntarily inhibited himself from the board's re-evaluation deliberations, the SBMA statement said.
